findings.title: The 2023 Record Year extended from January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2023.

findings.summary: PG&E operates the following UOG types: 1) hydroelectric, 2) fossil fuel, 3) battery energy storage, 4) solar, and 5) nuclear.

findings.summary: PG&E’s utility-owned hydroelectric portfolio consists of 61 powerhouses with 99 generating units with ancillary support facilities that include reservoirs, diversions, dams and water conveyance apparatus.

findings.summary: During the Record Year, PG&E owned, operated and maintained three fossil fuel generating stations, one battery storage energy project, and 10 ground- mounted PV solar stations.

findings.title: PG&E’s Gateway Generation Station, which is a fossil fuel generating facility…
findings.summary: PG&E’s Gateway Generation Station, which is a fossil fuel generating facility, experienced one forced outage during the Record Year.

findings.title: PG&E’s Humbolt Bay Generating Station, a fossil fuel generating facility, exp…
findings.summary: PG&E’s Humbolt Bay Generating Station, a fossil fuel generating facility, experienced 12 forced outages during the Record Year.

findings.summary: During August 2023, Humbolt Bay Generating Station unit 6 was forced out of service because the engine water pump bearings failed.

findings.title: PG&E owns the Elkhorn Battery Storage facility located in Monterey County.
findings.summary: PG&E owns the Elkhorn Battery Storage facility located in Monterey County.

findings.summary: On February 6, 2023, the Elkhorn Battery Storage facility was forced out of service for 45 hours while Tesla performed an emergency critical control system update for the site controller and tested the facility following the changes to the control system.

findings.title: PG&E’s PV generating facilities were operated at only 70.7 percent of expecte…
findings.summary: PG&E’s PV generating facilities were operated at only 70.7 percent of expected output because CAISO requested that PG&E curtail output for economic dispatch purposes. Otherwise, PG&E’s PV output would have achieved 81.9 percent of expected output.

findings.title: PG&E owns and operates the Diablo Canyon Nuclear Power Plant.
findings.summary: PG&E owns and operates the Diablo Canyon Nuclear Power Plant.

findings.summary: There were no forced outages at the Diablo Canyon Nuclear Power Plant during the Record Year.

findings.summary: PG&E’s testimony demonstrates that it operated Diablo Canyon Nuclear Power Plant in a reasonable manner during the Record Year.

findings.title: PG&E is in the process of conducting cause evaluations on the outages at the …
findings.summary: PG&E is in the process of conducting cause evaluations on the outages at the Belden and Caribou 1 Powerhouse outages and two maintenance outages at Diablo Canyon Nuclear Power Plant during the Record Year.

findings.title: During the Record Year, PG&E managed 482 and settled 485 energy contracts. Ne…
findings.summary: During the Record Year, PG&E managed 482 and settled 485 energy contracts. Net energy and RA payments totaled roughly $2.5 billion. PG&E also managed 112 contracts for projects that began delivery or achieved commercial operation, entered into 50 contract amendments, and settled disputes resulting in the collection of roughly $11.4 million in damages.

findings.summary: The evidentiary record in this proceeding supports a finding that PG&E satisfied the Commission’s requirements for the purchase and sale of RA capacity consistent with PG&E’s BPP.

findings.summary: In 2023, no customers took service under the Regional Renewable Choice program tariff.

findings.summary: The Community Solar Green Tariff program engages communities in developing solar projects within five miles of the participating customer’s community, or within 40 miles in the San Joaquin Valley pilot community.
